[HYP] Desktop key storage: migration from deprecated path may leave sensitive file with weak permissions
class: MISCONFIG
asset: apps/desktop/src/common/node/key-storage/index.ts (FileSystemKeyStorage)
confidence: 45
reasoning: Key storage file is written with `fileModeInternalObjectIfPosix()` (0600 on POSIX, empty on Windows). On Windows, file permissions are not enforced — the `keystorage.bin` and `keystorage.password.bin` files could be accessible to other processes/users. The password file uses `electron.safeStorage` which has OS-level protection, but the key storage file itself is only protected by the user's password (Argon2id).
evidence_needed: Confirm Windows file permission behavior — does `writeFile` without mode still create accessible files? Check if the password file (`keystorage.password.bin`) provides sufficient protection on Windows.
verify_steps: HUMAN_ONLY: Test on Windows target — check file permissions of `keystorage.bin` and `keystorage.password.bin` after app creation; attempt to read from another process.
impact: On Windows, an attacker with local access could read the encrypted key storage file. Argon2id password provides protection but offline brute-force is possible if password is weak. Severity: medium (local attack, requires access).
testability: HUMAN_ONLY
